newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds pulled lower by French election result.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds pulled lower by French election result.

text.p: Irish bonds were marked down on Monday in line with other peripheral markets after a surprise win for the left in the first round of France's elections, but dealers said there was no selling pressure and trade was extremely quiet due to a holiday in Britain.
"Prices were marked down at the open today, because if we see the left winning in the second round next week the prospects for economic and monetary union (EMU) will suffer," one dealer said.
"Worries about EMU hit peripheral markets like ours especially hard and we won't see too many people eager to buy Ireland until the second round is out of the way," he said.
Most of France's 577 National Assembly seats will be decided in the second round of the election on June 1.
By 1515 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was 25p weaker at 101.95 to yield 5.98 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 35p at 108.60 to yield 6.71 percent.
"We've seen hardly any trade at all, with the UK out on holiday," another dealer said. "But while we have uncertainty in France, Ireland will be hard pressed to make much headway."
